We require: egg albumin dispersion in a test tube, NaOH solution, 1% CuSO[sub]4[/sub] solution, test tube holder, rack, droppers and a Bunsen burner.
NaOH
1% Copper Sulphate
Take a small quantity NaOH solution using a dropper.
Add it to the egg albumin dispersion taken in a test tube.
Using another dropper, add a few drops of 1% copper sulphate solution to the test tube.
Remove the test tube from the rack using the test tube holder.
Heat the contents of the test tube over the burner for a few minutes.
In the presence of alkali, proteins react with copper (II) ions to form a violet colored complex called biuret.

We require egg albumin dispersion in a test tube, Ninhydrin solution, test tube holder, rack, dropper and a Bunsen burner.
Ninhydrin solution
Take a few drops of Ninhydrin solution using a dropper.
Add it to the egg albumin dispersion taken in a test tube.
Remove the test tube from the rack using a test tube holder.

Proteins react with ninhydrin reagent to form an intense blue colored compound.

We require egg albumin dispersion in a test tube, Millon's reagent, test tube holder, rack, dropper and a Bunsen burner.
Millon's reagent
Take a few drops of Millon’s reagent using a dropper.
Add it to the egg albumin dispersion taken in a test tube.
A white precipitate is formed.
Remove the test tube from the rack using a test tube holder.
Then boil the contents of the test tube over a burner.
White precipitate changes to brick red on boiling, confirming the presence of proteins.
